cover letter
Experience coordinating events, meetings, or programs, including scheduling, vendor arrangements, logistics, and participant communications.

In this position, the Program Administrator provides administrative coordination and operational support for the Department of Gender and Womens Studies and the Institute for Gender and Sexuality Research, reporting to the Cluster Director of Administration. The Program Administrator coordinates departmental purchasing, financial transactions, facilities, space and equipment, student employee activities, and academic and public events. The Program Administrator supports visiting scholar programs, grant proposal preparation and reporting, fundraising and outreach initiatives, website updates, and administrative services for department leadership, faculty, students, and external constituents. This position serves as the public face of Gender and Womens Studies with oversight of the front office both locally and in terms of the general public, and is fully in-person.
Program Administration and Operations - 40%
Coordinates office refurbishments, space and room arrangements, key control, equipment and supply inventory, upkeep of audiovisual systems and the computer lab, and facilities service requests

Coordinates day-to-day administrative operations for the Gender and Womens Studies department, helping ensure office workflows, facilities, equipment, and supplies are maintained and departmental needs are addressed.
Processes and tracks departmental purchasing, honoraria, invoicing, and related financial transactions in accordance with established University procedures.
Serves as the primary departmental purchaser, coordinating purchase requests, maintaining supporting documentation, and following up on transactions to ensure timely processing.
Reconciles departmental purchasing card transactions and coordinates timely posting of expenses to the appropriate chartstrings.
Provides administrative assistance with grant and contract proposals by gathering information and contributing to non-technical sections and supporting documentation.
Coordinates website updates and works with department management and appropriate technical resources to address website issues.
Provides day-to-day direction, training, and task coordination for student employees performing front-office, transactional, and event-support duties.

Provides administrative support to the Department Chair, Vice Chair for Research, and Director of Administration, including coordinating requests, preparing materials, and following up on assigned tasks.
Attends faculty meetings and departmental events, maintains administrative records and reference information, and helps ensure continuity of departmental activities and procedures.
Coordinates departmental calendars, conference room reservations, and room access for meetings and events.
Provides administrative backup to the Cluster, as needed, averaging no more than two hours per month.
Participates in departmental committees and completes related administrative follow-up as assigned.
Coordinates the logistical arrangements for departmental academic and public events, conferences, meetings, and programs.
Arranges venues, catering, vendors, audiovisual support, publicity, materials, room setup, and breakdown in accordance with established plans, schedules, and budgets.
Coordinates event requirements with faculty, staff, students, service providers, and other participants; tracks deadlines and resolves routine logistical issues.
Prepares event correspondence, schedules, announcements, and other written materials using knowledge of departmental programs and established communication practices.
IGSR Administrative Support - 20%
Provides administrative and logistical support to the Institute for Gender and Sexuality Research (IGSR) within the Department of Gender & Women's Studies.
Coordinates outreach activities and supports the receipt, tracking, and processing of program applications in accordance with established procedures.

Coordinates administrative onboarding activities for visiting scholars, visiting student researchers, and postdoctoral scholars, including collecting documentation and communicating applicable requirements.
Coordinates the day-to-day administrative needs of the IGSR computer lab, including equipment, supplies, access, and facilities requests.
Development and Outreach Support - 15%
Provides administrative support for departmental fundraising campaigns, including Big Give and DEWGS alumni campaigns; tracks donations and maintains related records.
Assists with grant proposals for competitive and non-competitive funding opportunities by gathering information, coordinating inputs, and preparing supporting materials.
Assists principal investigators with drafting and compiling information for external funding reports, including reports to the Chau Hoi Shuen and Mellon Foundations.
Coordinates administrative and logistical components of outreach projects, including newsletters, GWS Café, and alumni and donor communications.
Professional Development - 5%
Participates in career development workshops, classes, conferences, and collaborations through campus-sponsored and external resources
Demonstrated ability to coordinate multiple administrative projects, monitor deadlines, maintain records, and ensure timely completion of assigned activities.
Ability to prepare and edit professional correspondence, reports, announcements, and other administrative materials.
Thorough knowledge of financial administrative procedures and processes, including reconciling transactions, purchasing, invoices, reimbursements, or related expenditures.
Requires good verbal and written communication skills, active listening, critical thinking, multitasking, and time management skills.
Requires interpersonal and work leadership skills to provide guidance to other nonexempt personnel.
Ability to work independently, solve problems, set priorities, and take initiative in executing tasks with attention and accuracy.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite software and/or the ability to learn.
Familiarity with UC and campus policies and/or the ability to learn.
